newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends lower after heavy fund selling.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends lower after heavy fund selling.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures settled weaker but above session lows, pressured mostly by technically driven fund selling, floor sources said.
May cotton closed down 0.85 cent at 74.78 cents a lb, traded from 75.75 to 74.50 cents. Spot March went out 0.93 lower at 73.05 cents, while the outer contracts settled down 0.74 to 0.08 cent.
Volume was estimated at 14,000 lots, up from Monday's official 5,189 lots.

A handful of factors contributed to the day's weakness. The failure of May to pierce its overhead target of 76.20 cents in recent days signaled the need for prices to consolidate before moving higher, said Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc.

Certificated stocks, meantime, rose to 193,745 bales as of March 3, adding pressure to an already stressed market. And with a strong dollar, prices may have retreated in search of export business amid a dearth of sales in recent days.
Heavy rains in the Mississippi Delta have raised the possibility that the ground will remain too wet to plant corn in mid-March, thereby diverting land to cotton, which is planted later.
"An extremely wet spring could mean more acres cotton," Smith Barney vice president David Brandon, said.
Previously, market sources expected higher prices in other cash crops coupled with the flexibility to plant a varienty of crops under the 1996 Freedem to Farm bill, to slash planted cotton area.
USDA will release its first estimate of planted acreage for 1997/98, on March 31.
